summary: Configured centralized logging: node2 runs a simulated 'inventory' app (OpenRC service) that logs via syslog; rsyslog on node2 forwards those messages (disk-queued, infinite retry) to node1 over TCP 514; rsyslog on node1 receives and persists them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Verified live delivery, then restarted node1 and node2 sequentially (boot_id changed for both), confirming rsyslog/inventory services auto-start at boot, previously persisted log data survives, and log flow resumes/queued messages flush after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes (Alpine 3.23, OpenRC, busybox syslogd default) and confirmed no pre-existing inventory app
Installed rsyslog via apk on node1 and node2
Stopped and de-registered busybox syslog service on both nodes; enabled rsyslog at boot on both
Created simulated inventory application (/usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh) and OpenRC service (/etc/init.d/inventory) on node2, enabled at boot
Configured node2 rsyslog forwarding rule (/etc/rsyslog.d/inventory-forward.conf) to send programname=inventory messages to node1:514/TCP with a disk-assisted, infinite-retry queue
Configured node1 rsyslog to listen on TCP/UDP 514 (imtcp/imudp) and write messages from node2's IP with programname=inventory to /var/log/inventory/node2.log (/etc/rsyslog.d/inventory.conf)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status, log tail) for both nodes
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, rsyslog auto-started and listening, and buffered node2 messages flushed into node2.log
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, rsyslog and inventory services auto-started, and fresh log events resumed appearing in node1's node2.log

evidence.requirement: node2 inventory app logs are forwarded to and persisted on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: After configuring forwarding, node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log shows live inventory events (seq=1,2,3) arriving from node2 within seconds

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart (rsyslog listening, receiving data)
evidence.summary: rsyslog listening on TCP/UDP 514 with boot_id 3e71ddf1-36d5-400a-a5ab-24a7be749a93 captured before restart; node2.log had 4 lines

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart (inventory + rsyslog running)
evidence.summary: boot_id 00dd194a-8b4b-40e8-b35c-3e86d420fb2b captured; inventory and rsyslog both status started

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot scheduled and acknowledged before disconnect; after polling, boot_id changed to 09f36add-e67d-4e3f-8b92-ddd37c1e1194, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery: service auto-start and data/flow integrity
evidence.summary: rsyslog auto-started at boot, listening on 514, and previously-queued node2 messages (seq 9-13) plus prior file content were present in node2.log, confirming both persistence and queue-based recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot scheduled and acknowledged before disconnect; after polling, boot_id changed to fb3b316a-5971-4c0f-9e81-189357e34add, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery: inventory app and forwarding auto-start, flow resumes
evidence.summary: Both rsyslog and inventory services auto-started after boot (new PIDs), and fresh inventory log events (seq=1 through 8 of the new run) appeared in node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log shortly after node2 came back up
